<reason>Side A (CON) won by turning B's already-exists defense into a difference in kind: SSN proves little and scattered copies cannot be queried live, while a blessed signature is instantly trusted everywhere, concentrating payoff, enabling live logging and function creep via incentives and SSN history. A answered pressure directly with finite vs generative harm and delay-as-mandate, and weighed diffuse compensable fraud against permanent indexed traceability. B's statute caps and parallel-door reply never solved future expansion or revocation checks.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's concentration and revocability counter — SSN cobbles forgeries vs master key, revocation freezes victim, offline still needs enrollment/revocation and verifier logs — most damaged B's live route that revocable selective disclosure is strictly better than the leaky analog baseline.</best_rebuttal>
